$comment: OURS. One declared lease row, read by `magus ledger register --stdin` and mirroring the fields the magus_ledger tool's put accepts. Mirrors ledger.Row; TestRowSchemaMatchesTheStruct fails when either side grows a field the other lacks.
title: magus lease row

schema_version.description: The row shape this record is written in. Required: a version this magus does not know is rejected by name.

id.description: The lease's identity within the plan, and the key a second register replaces on. Letters, digits and -_./: only, at most 128 characters.

parent.description: The lease this one was handed out under. Empty for a lease the root declared.

goal.description: The goal and its observable acceptance criteria, as one block of text.

checkpoint.description: The working state this lease is handed, as `magus vcs checkpoint -o name` prints it.

owned_paths.description: The declared write lane. Empty on a read-only row by design.

forbidden_paths.description: Paths inside the lane this lease may not write.

focus.description: The declared READ lane, widened to those projects' dependencies by the guard. Empty means owned_paths stands in.

depends_on.description: Lease ids that must land before this one.

tier.description: The effort tier the work was matched to. A free string: hosts name their tiers differently.

target.description: The target this lease's one check runs, carrying a `spell::` filter when the row names one.

project.description: The project it runs in. Defaults to the workspace root.

args.description: What is forwarded past `--` to the tool the target runs. Not compared when evidence is bound: the output store records a run by target and project and holds no argv.

check.description: The one check this lease runs. Acceptance binds a worker's evidence to it.

validation.description: The check as a rendered `magus run <target> <project> [-- args]` line, accepted in place of `check` for one release and parsed into it. Sending both is refused.

state.description: The row's lifecycle position, empty for a row that has not said where it stands. no_return is a lease that never reported, which is not a failure.

read_only.description: A lease that gathers evidence and writes nothing, so empty owned paths are correct rather than missing.
